newsitem.title: UK: Number of VLCCs in dry dock up sharply - Intertank.
newsitem.headline: Number of VLCCs in dry dock up sharply - Intertank.

text.p: The number of very large crude carriers (VLCCs) in dry dock rose sharply over the last three years, from 104 in 1994 to 122 in 1995 and 158 last year, Intertanko said on Tuesday.
The international tanker grouping said this was a "natural trend" considering the number of VLCCs that were built around 1976 and are due for their fourth Enhanced Special Periodical Survey (ESPS).
The Oslo-based organisation said that not only had the number of VLCCs in dock risen strongly, but the number of days they remained there had increased from an average of 23 in 1995 to 31 last year.
The average for all tankers had risen by one day to 24.
"This may be due to the implementation of the ESPS and a stricter practice by Class," Intertanko said in its March market report.
